title: Sand Trap

introduction.definition: A sand trap removes sand and other solids from well fluids or process streams. A tangential inlet sets up a swirl that throws the sand to the wall; it slides into the conical bottom while the cleaned fluid turns and leaves through the central vortex finder. The accumulated sand is dumped periodically.
applications: Protection of chokes, separators and pumps
key_points: Sand dumped by ΔP or level
Erosion-resistant materials at inlet and dump

pressure.title: Swirl throws sand to the wall
pressure.description: The tangential inlet sets up a swirl. Dense sand grains are thrown outward to the wall and slide down into the cone, while the cleaned fluid turns and leaves through the central vortex finder. Sand removal protects chokes, valves and separators from erosion. The rising ΔP / sand level triggers a dump (flush) of the cone — always under controlled conditions because of the erosive, pressurised discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Sand Trap — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Sand Trap.
A sand trap removes sand and other solids from well fluids or process streams.
A tangential inlet sets up a swirl that throws the sand to the wall; it slides into the conical bottom while the cleaned fluid turns and leaves through the central vortex finder.
The accumulated sand is dumped periodically.
Typical applications include wellhead and production flowlines; protection of chokes, separators and pumps; water injection and produced-water systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Sand Trap.
Monitor ΔP / sand level; dump.
UT thickness at inlet.
Replace wear parts and dump valve.
Watch for erosion: wall thinning. Common cause: high velocity sand.
Watch for dump valve failure: sand overflow downstream. Common cause: erosion of valve.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
